new_jobs.description:
About Summit

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.
Summit’s Team Is Inspired To Touch And Help Change Lives Through Summit’s Clinical Studies In The Field Of Oncology. Summit Has Multiple Global Phase 3 Clinical Studies, Including
Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)

HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.
HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.
HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC)

HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland.
Overview Of Role

Summit is seeking a highly motivated Sr. Clinical Data Scientist to join our growing team. This role will be instrumental in advancing our technology-enabled and data-driven clinical data review and study monitoring strategy through automation, analytics, and cross-functional data support.
The ideal candidate will be proficient in R and/or Python and apply these skills across clinical data domains to enhance processes, increase efficiency, and elevate data quality. A strong focus on workflow optimization, coupled with a passion for implementing technical solutions in a fast-paced pharmaceutical environment, will be essential for success.
Role And Responsibilities

Develop clinical study reports, dashboards, and data visualizations using R or Python.
Partner closely with the Data Management team to implement data-monitoring or reconciliation listings and edit checks that support ongoing data review.
Collaborate with Clinical Operations to generate study metrics and identify potential site-level risks.
Communicate requirements clearly with vendors, author and curate specs, and ensure the results delivered by vendors.
Perform data wrangling and data processing in R/Python to support the summarization and interpretation of clinical trial data.
Build ETL pipelines in a Windows environment to automate clinical data workflows and streamline clinical programming activities.
Develop and maintain reusable R packages for data cleaning, transformation, and validation.
Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready documentation and specs for all programming activities.

Required

Experience, Education and Specialized Knowledge and Skills:

Master’s or Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Biostatistics, Computer Science, Life Sciences, or a related field
Minimum 5-7 years Pharmaceutical/Biotech programming experience.
Proficiency in R or Python, and experience with data visualization tools (e.g., Shiny, Spotfire, Tableau) and R packages
Understanding of EDC and clinical trial processes
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and translate non-technical requirements into technical solutions
The ability to work well under pressure and shift priorities, both as a team leader and as a team member.
Ability to communicate clearly both oral and written.

Preferred

Experience with maintaining data visualization systems
Experience with Github
Prior experience in oncology or complex therapeutic areas
Ability to proactively identify and address project uncertainties to minimize risk.
Strong problem solving and analytical skills.

This is the pay for this position
Pay Transparency
$148,000 - $188,000 USD
Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor. The total compensation package for this position may also include bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable variable compensation.
Summit does not accept referrals from employment businesses and/or employment agencies in respect of the vacancies posted on this site. All employment businesses/agencies are required to contact Summit’s Talent Acquisition team at recruiting@smmttx.com to obtain prior written authorization before referring any candidates to Summit.

We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training or promotion or any other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status.

new_jobs.title: Staff Research Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Description de l'entreprise

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

Description du poste

As a Staff Researcher, you will work on research questions that most AI labs simply do not have access to. ServiceNow AI Research is chartered to build the future of enterprise agentic AI, from a rare vantage point: we see how agents actually behave, inside complex enterprise environments, at scale.

You will contribute to research initiatives on how agents accumulate and reuse tacit knowledge, learn and improve continuously, and on their resilience, their safety, and the privacy of the data they handle. These are the real obstacles to enterprise agentic deployment today, and they surface in operational reality well before they appear in the literature.

While much of the AI and NLP community concentrates on core agent capabilities, our team explores the dimensions that determine real adoption: safety mechanisms, threat detection, privacy guarantees, and responsible AI practices. You will have the freedom to publish and advance the state of the art, with the rare advantage of testing your hypotheses against real deployments rather than against benchmarks.

Qualifications

PhD in computer science, machine learning, or a related field, or equivalent research experience
2 or more years of research experience post-PhD, a significant portion of it in an industrial setting or in direct contact with deployed systems
Established publication record at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or equivalents), with contributions recognized as influential in your field
Demonstrated track record of setting/executing research agenda, not only executing one: you have chosen problems before the community turned to them, and you can explain why
Experience working on cross-disciplinary teams or projects collaborating with researchers and engineers
Strong software development skills: you write, maintain, and optimize high-quality research code, and you know what it takes for a result to survive the move into production
Advanced use of agentic tools in your own research practice, and a willingness to advance the team's practices in this area
Demonstrated ability to influence technical decisions beyond your own team, particularly with product and engineering teams
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical work to non-specialist audiences and to executives

Nice to have

Expertise in one or more of the following areas: agent memory and tacit knowledge, continual learning, safety and alignment, security and threat detection, privacy, agent evaluation
Experience with AI systems operating in real enterprise environments, with the compliance, governance, and scale constraints that entails
Contributions to open source software, datasets, or evaluation benchmarks used by the community
Scientific service roles: program committees, editorial work, workshop organization
Academic collaborations or supervision of doctoral students
Fluency in French, or interest in learning it, in a bilingual Montreal work environment

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $202,500 - $354,400
, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

I'm Rahul
from Floga Technologies

Dallas: TX or CA (Hybrid)

Duration: Long Term

Experience: 10+ Years

Anthology Solutions Inc. is recruiting experienced Software Engineering Leads for an enterprise client's engineering team. This Java-only role requires deep enterprise backend engineering experience and hands-on expertise in Agentic AI across the software development lifecycle (SDLC). You will lead the design and delivery of scalable, high-throughput applications using Java, Spring Boot, microservices, and event-driven architecture, while driving adoption of AI agents and AI-augmented development practices across the SDLC. Candidates must demonstrate competency in both Java and AI, with an AI mindset for software development. .NET-only profiles do not meet this requirement. The roles are hybrid and based primarily in the Dallas Fort Worth area. A limited number of San Francisco-based candidates with exceptional profiles may also be considered. The engagement starts as a 12-month contract with the potential to convert to full-time employment with the client or to be extended. C2C engagements are preferred; W-2 employment through Anthology may also be considered. Anthology represents candidates for these openings, and all applications are submitted to Anthology.

Responsibilities

Design and build AI agents and agentic workflows, including orchestration, tool/function calling, state and memory management, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and human-in-the-loop controls.

Integrate AI agents with enterprise applications, APIs, event streams, databases, and internal knowledge sources.

Establish standards for prompt/context engineering, model selection, evaluation, guardrails, observability, security, and sensitive-data handling.

Lead architecture and code reviews, mentor engineers, and define engineering standards for distributed systems and AI-assisted development.

Own non-functional requirements including performance, scalability, availability, resilience, security, and cost efficiency.

10+ years of software engineering experience, including 2+ years in a Lead, Staff, Principal, or similar technical role.

Proficiency and hands-on experience with an agentic SDLC to generate, review, and test code.

Proficiency and hands-on experience building agentic AI solutions using technologies such as LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, Spring AI, or MCP-based tooling.

Strong hands-on experience reviewing AI-generated code and designs for quality, security, performance, and maintainability.

Strong experience modernizing legacy enterprise applications using AI-assisted development techniques.

Strong experience designing and operating high-throughput, scalable microservices and distributed systems in production.

Strong experience with Kafka or comparable event-streaming/messaging platforms and event-driven architecture.

Deep hands-on expertise in Java 11/17/21 and Spring Boot, with experience in Spring Cloud, Spring Data, and Spring Security.

Strong knowledge of REST/gRPC, Java concurrency, thread pools, caching, resilience patterns, and distributed-system design.

Strong fundamentals in system design, data structures, databases, networking, concurrency, cloud, and CI/CD.

new_jobs.description:
Responsibilities

PGC (Professionally Generated Content) is one of TikTok's key business directions. By providing professional content, PGC helps meet users' needs for high-quality, trustworthy, and diverse content consumption. The PGC business consists of several core modules, including creator growth strategies, post and content management tools, content distribution strategies, creator monetization strategies, and OGC verticals.

As a Data Scientist on the Data team, you will contribute to analyses of user behavior, product features, and the content ecosystem. You will help the team understand user needs, evaluate product and strategy impact, and translate data insights into actionable business recommendations. You will work closely with Product, Operations, Engineering, and Machine Learning Engineering teams, while growing your capabilities in analytics, experimentation, and business judgment through real product challenges.

Responsibilities
- Participate in data analysis across PGC content and product areas, exploring supply and demand dynamics, user behaviors, and the creator ecosystem to identify testable business questions and growth opportunities.
- Support the design and maintenance of core metrics, dashboards, and analytical definitions to improve continuous business tracking and decision-making efficiency.
- Partner with Product, Operations, Algorithm, and Engineering teams to support strategy evaluation and optimization across recommendation, distribution, content consumption, and creator growth.
- Contribute to A/B test design and result analysis; evaluate product features, strategy changes, and trending operations; support metric anomaly investigation and root-cause analysis.
- Validate business hypotheses through analysis, experimentation, and other scientific methods, and deliver clear, actionable findings and recommendations.
- Drive analytical workstreams with guidance from other teammates and grow toward independent ownership of product and business domains.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualification(s)
- Bachelor’s degree or above in Data Science, Statistics, Econometrics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or related fields
- 1+ years of experience in data analysis, data science, or relevant internship/full-time roles.
- Solid foundation in statistics; understanding of A/B testing, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and common analytical methods
- Proficient in SQL; able to use Python or R for data processing, basic modeling, and visualization.
- Strong structured thinking, with the ability to break business problems into analyzable and testable data questions.
- Good communication skills, with the ability to clearly present analytical process, findings, and recommendations, and a willingness to learn proactively in cross-functional collaboration.

Preferred Qualification(s)
- Experience or coursework in causal inference is a plus.
- Interest in content products, recommendation systems, creator ecosystems, or growth strategies; experience in news, content communities, recommendation, or user growth projects is a plus.
- Experience with overseas markets, or cross-region projects is a plus.
- Strong curiosity, self-drive, and learning agility; able to iterate on analytical methods and business understanding through feedback.

new_jobs.description:
Job Details

Job Description:

Intel is transforming to meet the demands of a rapidly changing world. We design and deliver industryleading technology that powers data centers, enables AI, and drives the future of computing. Join a team building the software and platforms developers use to deliver performance at scale.

The Senior AI Developer Relations Advocate serves as the primary owner of the example applications developers copy when they build agentic and retrieval augmented generation solutions on Intel's current and future data center platforms.

This role builds and maintains production quality demos, blueprints, and workshop repositories on open libraries, including vLLM, SGLang, and Intel Inference Microservices, and on Open Source agent frameworks, including LangChain and MCP. The role treats every example as a product. Each one is pinned and reproducible, tested in CI from a clean machine, documented for a developer with no prior context, and runnable unmodified on Intel data center platforms.

The role leads flagship workshops and livecoding sessions at conferences, hackathons, and customer sites, and converts what developers hit in those rooms into fixes in the examples, the upstream libraries, and the product. Strong hands on Python engineering, depth in inference serving and agent frameworks, visible opensource engagement, and the ability to teach and present to developers live are essential.

Responsibilities

Own the agentic and retrieval augmented generation example applications for the AI software stack on data center platforms, including inference microservices and the agentic toolkit.
Build and ship production quality demos, blueprints, and workshop repositories that developers can clone, run, and copy into their own projects.
Build on open libraries and agent frameworks, including vLLM, SGLang, Intel Inference Microservices, LangChain, and MCP, and keep the examples current as those libraries and models change.
Test every example in CI from a clean machine so it runs on a first attempt and stays reproducible.
Lead flagship workshops, hackathons, and livecoding sessions at developer events and customer sites.
Contribute upstream to the open libraries and agent frameworks the examples depend on.
Convert what developers hit in workshops, issues, and customer engagements into fixes in the examples, the documentation, and the product.
Partner with engineering, product, and developer advocates so each new capability ships with a working example application.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree with 4 years of experience in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field or equivalent practical experience.
Experience building agentic applications with agent frameworks and familiar with tool calling protocols such as LangChain and MCP.
Experience with open inference libraries such as vLLM or SGLang, including serving models behind compatible endpoints.
Experience building retrieval augmented generation applications end to end, including retrieval, embedding, and serving components.
Track record of publishing reference applications or samples that other developers run, with visible open source contributions preferred.
Prior experience in Developer Relations, Developer Advocacy, or a similar role, including leading workshops or livecoding sessions for developer audiences.

Excellent written and verbal communication with technical audiences.
Ability to translate developer feedback into example applications, documentation, and product improvements.
Strong hands on Python engineering with the AI software stack, especially CPU based and heterogeneous AI inference.

new_jobs.title: AI Engineer 4
new_jobs.description:
At Capital One, we are creating responsible and reliable AI systems, changing banking for good. For years, Capital One has been an industry leader in using machine learning to create real-time, personalized customer experiences. Our investments in technology infrastructure and world-class talent — along with our deep experience in machine learning — position us to be at the forefront of enterprises leveraging AI. From informing customers about unusual charges to answering their questions in real time, our applications of AI & ML are bringing humanity and simplicity to banking. We are committed to continuing to build world-class applied science and engineering teams to deliver our industry leading capabilities with breakthrough product experiences and scalable, high-performance AI infrastructure. At Capital One, you will help bring the transformative power of emerging AI capabilities to reimagine how we serve our customers and businesses who have come to love the products and services we build.

Team Description:

The Intelligent Foundations and Experiences (IFX) team is at the center of bringing our vision for AI at Capital One to life. We work hand-in-hand with our partners across the company to advance the state of the art in science and AI engineering, and we build and deploy proprietary solutions that are central to our business and deliver value to millions of customers. Our AI models and platforms empower teams across Capital One to enhance their products with the transformative power of AI, in responsible and scalable ways for the highest leverage impact.

What You’ll Do:

Partner with a cross-functional team of engineers, research scientists, technical program managers, and product managers to deliver AI-powered products that change how our associates work and how our customers interact with Capital One.
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support AI software components including foundation model training, large language model inference, agents and multi-agent workflows, similarity search, guardrails, model evaluation, experimentation, governance, and observability, etc.
Leverage a broad stack of Open Source and SaaS AI technologies such as AWS Ultraclusters, Huggingface, VectorDBs, PyTorch, and more.
Invent and introduce state-of-the-art foundation model optimization techniques to improve the performance — scalability, cost, latency, throughput — of large scale production AI systems.
Contribute to the technical vision and the long term roadmap of foundational AI systems at Capital One.
Own the end-to-end architecture for complex AI systems - ensuring maintainability, observability, and ethical alignment
Define and maintain service-level objectives (SLOs) for AI reliability, including latency, uptime, and model performance drift
Collaborate with infrastructure engineering to optimize GPU/TPU utilization and accelerate model inference pipelines
Lead cross-functional technical reviews for new AI system deployments, ensuring security, data governance, and compliance standards are met
Mentor Principal and Senior Associates on scalable design, performance tuning and research-to-production translation

The Ideal Candidate:

You love to build systems, take pride in the quality of your work, and also share our passion to do the right thing. You want to work on problems that will help change banking for good
Passion for staying abreast of the latest research, and an ability to intuitively understand scientific publications and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
You adapt quickly and thrive on bringing clarity to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and digging deep to uncover the root of problems and can articulate your findings concisely with clarity. You have the courage to share new ideas even when they are unproven
You are deeply Technical. You possess a strong foundation in engineering and mathematics, and your expertise in hardware, software, and AI enables you to see and exploit optimization opportunities that others miss
You are a resilient trailblazer who can forge new paths to achieve business goals when the route is unknown

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 4 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies, or a Master's degree in Computer Science, AI, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related fields plus at least 2 years of experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies
At least 4 years of experience programming with Python, Go, Scala, CUDA, or Java

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience leading development AI systems with tradeoff decisions around cost, latency, throughput and accuracy
6+ years of experience deploying scalable and responsible AI solutions on cloud platforms (e.g. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or equivalent private cloud)
Experience designing, developing, delivering, and supporting AI services
Experience developing AI and ML algorithms or technologies (e.g. LLM Inference, Similarity Search and VectorDBs, Guardrails, Memory) using Python, C++, C#, Java, CUDA, or Golang
Experience developing and applying state-of-the-art techniques for optimizing training and inference software to improve hardware utilization, latency, throughput, and cost
Experience in building agentic AI systems and agentic workflows
Passion for staying abreast of the latest AI research and AI systems, and judiciously apply novel techniques in production
Proficiency in designing distributed systems for model training, evaluation, and online inference at petabyte scale
Experience defining AI model governance processes, including producibility, lineage tracking, and automated retaining schedules
Demonstrated ability to influence architectural decisions across multiple AI product lines or platforms

new_jobs.title: Staff Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a member of the GTM team at Anthropic, you will be a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) who embeds directly with our most strategic customers and leads the technical direction of their AI adoption. Customers bring you in to lead, not only to implement: you decide what should be built, and then make sure it gets built well. You will work with customer teams to ship advanced AI applications that solve real world business problems, and guide the architecture and advisory work that surrounds those builds across an account.

Working closely with our Research, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll combine engineering expertise, an understanding of frontier AI applications, and customer-facing skills to understand customer workflows and develop innovative solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.

You will sit at the frontier of enterprise AI deployments and help shape our forward-deployed motion as it scales. We expect Staff FDEs to set direction under ambiguity and represent Anthropic at the highest level in customer environments. In this role, you guide architecture and build initiatives across workstreams, working directly with senior technical and business stakeholders and owning outcomes that span an account's roadmap.

You don't need to have shipped agents to production. You do need deep experience building and operating production systems, hands-on time with agents, and the judgment to lead architecture and advisory work with enterprise customers.

Responsibilities

Own technical strategy for a key account or vertical, in partnership with account and product teams.
Guide technical architecture and design decisions across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Lead discovery and advisory engagements independently, shaping scope and technical strategy before a build starts.
Lead engagements delivered with partners, setting the architecture and the quality bar for work you don't build yourself.
Review designs and unblock other FDEs on hard technical calls.
Represent Anthropic to senior technical and business stakeholders, including VPs and C-level, to align on strategy and de-risk delivery.
Own your engagements end to end: scope the work, sequence it, unblock it, anticipate security and procurement gates, and deliver production systems the customer can operate.
Work within customer systems to build production applications and agent components with Claude, and hand over systems the customer can run.
Identify and codify repeatable deployment patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams.
Build long term relationships with customers and proactively identify new opportunities for AI deployment throughout the lifecycle of an engagement.
Travel frequently (25%) to customer sites to build in person with customers.
Be a champion for Anthropic's mission in the field.

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

Position:
Data Scientist

Position Location:
Peterson Air Force Base (Colorado Springs, Colorado)

Position Description

A data scientist will have skills sets of both data analysts and data engineers. Data scientists are responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a data pipeline. In addition, data scientists shall interpret and analyze complex sets of data, as well as plan, execute, and manage ML projects with cloud-native platforms and advanced ML solutions. They understand some of the most challenging processes, technologies, and can leverage a vast array of methodologies in the field, such as data mining, natural language programming, and machine learning.

Data scientists must have a combination of skills that include programming, mathematical modeling, statistics, and domain knowledge. They must combine an advanced math and statistics background with programming, domain knowledge, and communication skills to analyze data, create applied mathematical models, and present results in a form useful to the organization. They must also be able to understand and manipulate structured and unstructured large data sets, which requires proficiency in distributed SQL programming, relational and non-relational data queries, general programming languages (such as Python and R,) and machine learning techniques.

Experience

Interpret and analyze data using exploratory mathematic and statistical techniques based on the scientific method.
Coordinate research and analytic activities utilizing various data points (unstructured and structured) and employ programming to clean, massage, and organize the data
Experiment against data points, provide information based on experiment results and provide previously undiscovered solutions to command data challenges.
Coordinate with Data Engineers to build Data environments providing data identified by other data professionals
Apply and develop scientific methodology, statistics, and algorithms to discover and frame relevant problems, hypotheses, and opportunities.
Develop predictive and prescriptive modeling, natural language processing (NLP), Robotic Process Automation (RPA), text mining and processing, clustering, forecasting methods, and other advanced statistical techniques.
Design and automate processes to facilitate the manipulation and analysis of data. Manage and integrate data across dissimilar data sets. Analyze large-scale structured and unstructured data.
Use frameworks such as Spark and Hadoop to conduct large-scale data processing. Perform statistical modeling and create data visualizations using products like Tableau, Microsoft Power BI and R Shiny.
Research, design, and implement algorithms to solve complex problems. Program using R, Python (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas) or similar analytical languages.
Perform data engineering, data processing and modeling techniques using cloud-based data management, data science, and ML platforms such as Databricks, IBM Cloud Pak, Cloudera, and Snowflake.
Communicate complex concepts and hypothesis to a non-technical audience through digital storytelling.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in a STEM field is required. Master’s degree is preferred in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Computer Science, or related fields.
3-5 years data science experience required
Proficient with one or more programming languages (Java, C++, Python, R, etc.).
Proficient in Agile Development and Git Operations.
Demonstrated experience applying data science methods to real-world data problems.
TS/SCI clearance required

new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a member of the GTM team at Anthropic, you will be a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) who embeds directly with our most strategic customers and leads the technical direction of their AI adoption. Customers bring you in to lead, not only to implement: you decide what should be built, and then make sure it gets built well. You will work with customer teams to ship advanced AI applications that solve real world business problems, and guide the architecture and advisory work that surrounds those builds across an account.

Working closely with our Research, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll combine engineering expertise, an understanding of frontier AI applications, and customer-facing skills to understand customer workflows and develop innovative solutions that address complex business challenges while maintaining our high standards for safety and reliability.

You will sit at the frontier of enterprise AI deployments and help shape our forward-deployed motion as it scales. We expect Staff FDEs to set direction under ambiguity and represent Anthropic at the highest level in customer environments. In this role, you guide architecture and build initiatives across workstreams, working directly with senior technical and business stakeholders and owning outcomes that span an account's roadmap.

You don't need to have shipped agents to production. You do need deep experience building and operating production systems, hands-on time with agents, and the judgment to lead architecture and advisory work with enterprise customers.

Responsibilities

Own technical strategy for a key account or vertical, in partnership with account and product teams.
Guide technical architecture and design decisions across multiple concurrent workstreams.
Lead discovery and advisory engagements independently, shaping scope and technical strategy before a build starts.
Lead engagements delivered with partners, setting the architecture and the quality bar for work you don't build yourself.
Review designs and unblock other FDEs on hard technical calls.
Represent Anthropic to senior technical and business stakeholders, including VPs and C-level, to align on strategy and de-risk delivery.
Own your engagements end to end: scope the work, sequence it, unblock it, anticipate security and procurement gates, and deliver production systems the customer can operate.
Work within customer systems to build production applications and agent components with Claude, and hand over systems the customer can run.
Identify and codify repeatable deployment patterns and contribute insights back to our Product and Engineering teams.
Build long term relationships with customers and proactively identify new opportunities for AI deployment throughout the lifecycle of an engagement.
Travel frequently (25%) to customer sites to build in person with customers.
Be a champion for Anthropic's mission in the field.

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

Deep system design and problem decomposition skills: you can walk into a discovery conversation with only a business problem and leave with a defensible technical strategy for a secure, production-ready design inside a complex enterprise environment of legacy systems, with identity and access, and compliance requirements.
Experience in a senior technical, customer facing role such as Forward Deployed Engineer, or as a Tech Lead with consulting or product experience. Former technical founders are also encouraged to apply.
A track record as the person a team turns to on ambiguous technical calls, whether through architecture review, pairing, or informal mentorship.
A track record of directly influencing senior technical and business stakeholders, including VP and C-level, in complex organizations.
Extensive experience building and operating production systems. Hands-on experience with LLMs and agents is expected. Side projects and prototypes count.
Strong programming skills with proficiency in Python (and ideally in one or more additional languages like TypeScript, Java, etc), experience shipping production applications, and everyday use of AI coding tools with the judgment to review and steer.
Experience leading advisory and architecture-review engagements as well as hands-on builds, and running them end to end.
High agency with an ability to navigate ambiguity present in complex organizations, and the learning velocity to pick up new domains and tools fast.
Passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI systems through creative technical applications.
A background in financial services, healthcare/life sciences, or another enterprise vertical are nice to have.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$280,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. new_jobs.description:
Position:
Product Engineer, AI & Automation

Department:
Digital Experience

Role Overview:
The Operational Efficiency team works with departments across the organization to reduce manual effort in daily operations. This role is the team's primary builder. You will take processes that are currently slow, repetitive, or error-prone and turn them into working automations, applying AI capabilities where they fit the problem.

Most of your time will be spent building: writing code, connecting systems, designing and testing agents, and maintaining what you have already shipped. Requirements will reach you as problems rather than finished specifications, so you will work directly with the teams whose processes you are automating to understand how the work is performed before deciding what to build.

We are looking for someone with five or more years of experience who has delivered automations that people depend on daily and who has supported them over time.

What you’ll get to do:

Build

Design and build automations across operational workflows, including data movement, document handling, reporting, intake and routing, and notifications.
Connect existing systems using REST APIs, webhooks, scheduled jobs, and integration platforms, working within the organization's current technology stack wherever possible.
Build components that use large language models where they are the right tool for the problem, including extraction from unstructured documents, classification, routing, summarization, and drafting. Design the prompts, test them against representative data, and define the accuracy required before launching.
Determine where human review is required, set confidence thresholds that route uncertain cases to staff, and define what happens when the model produces incorrect output.
Handle supporting work with the same care as the build itself, including data validation, idempotency, credential management, environment separation, and documentation sufficient for another engineer to take over.

Define and scope

Work with department leads to document current-state processes and identify automation candidates, quantifying the time and cost each process consumes today.
Assess feasibility and recommend alternatives when a process change or a configuration change in an existing system would solve the problem more effectively than a new automation.
Translate operational needs into technical requirements and divide work into phases that deliver value early.
Set clear expectations with stakeholders on accuracy, exception handling, and scope. This matters especially for AI-assisted steps, where acceptable error rates should be agreed in advance.

Own and maintain

Own each automation through its full lifecycle, including monitoring, response when upstream systems change, iteration as processes evolve, and retirement once it is no longer needed.
Build in monitoring and alerting so that failures surface quickly instead of going unnoticed.
Maintain documentation and runbooks so that support does not depend on a single person.
Track and report impact, including hours returned, error rates, cycle time, and usage.

Support and enable others

Train and support staff who want to build simple automations on their own, extending the reach of the team.
Contribute to the team's standards and patterns, including guidelines on what organizational data may be sent to external AI services.

Qualifications

Required

5+ years of professional experience building automations, integrations, or internal tools.
Strong Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript skills, with experience writing code that other engineers have maintained.
Substantial experience with REST APIs, authentication patterns, webhooks, and system-to-system integration.
Hands-on experience building with large language models, including prompt design, structured output, and methods for evaluating output quality.
Working knowledge of SQL and experience with inconsistent or incomplete operational data.
Proven ability to work with non-technical stakeholders, including gathering requirements, managing expectations, and supporting adoption.
Good judgment about which processes are appropriate for candidates for automation, and which are not.

Preferred

Experience with integration or workflow platforms such as Workato, Make, n8n, Zapier, Power Automate, Airflow, or Temporal.
Experience with document processing, OCR, or extraction from unstructured sources.
Experience in a comparable operational environment where automations touch finance, HR, or customer-facing workflows.
Familiarity with data governance and access controls in environments that handle sensitive records.

Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Everpure is looking for a Senior Services Solution Architect to lead the development of Advanced Services capabilities across AI data platforms and production AI, helping customers turn enterprise data and AI use cases into validated, production-ready solutions.

This is a senior, innovation-focused Professional Services role responsible for identifying customer and market opportunities, shaping technical approaches, validating them through customer engagements and pilots, and maturing successful concepts into scalable, repeatable services and capabilities.

You will act as a senior Advanced Services technical authority for AI, working closely with our AI pre-sales teams, Product Engineering, partners, and delivery organizations. You will combine strong AI and data architecture expertise with hands-on experimentation to help customers progress from use-case definition and prototype through data preparation, model and retrieval evaluation, integration, and production.

The role sits at the intersection of AI, enterprise data and customer execution. It is not a generic AI application-development role, nor an infrastructure-only role. The focus is applying AI to real customer problems, proving what works, and establishing the data, architecture and operational foundations required to run it successfully in production.

What You'll Do

Shape AI Services Strategy: Help define the Advanced Services strategy and capabilities for AI, identifying customer needs, emerging use cases, technology trends, and opportunities to accelerate adoption.
Validate AI Requirements: Work with strategic customers to understand AI use cases and translate them into the data, platform and services requirements necessary to move from concept to production.
Architect AI Data Solutions: Design architectures spanning enterprise data, preparation and transformation, retrieval, embeddings, vectorization, knowledge architectures, model integration, and AI consumption.
Drive DataStream Services: Develop discovery methodologies, corpus assessment, deployment patterns, reference architectures, sizing, retrieval optimization and production-readiness approaches around DataStream and associated AI data pipelines.
Lead Pilot-Led Innovation: Work in an FDE-style model with customers through discovery, prototype, MVP and pilot phases, iterating rapidly and turning successful approaches into scalable delivery capability.
Productionize AI Solutions: Help customers move from experimentation into production, addressing model and retrieval quality, performance, observability, governance, resiliency, operational readiness, and lifecycle requirements.
Bridge Pre-Sales and Delivery: Partner closely with AI FSAs, AI specialists, Product Engineering, partners, and delivery teams to transition emerging AI opportunities into executable customer engagements.
Influence Product and Services Direction: Capture learning from real customer deployments and create feedback loops into Product Engineering and the wider organization to improve products, architectures, and future services.
Accelerate Services Growth: Influence pipeline and strategic opportunities by translating complex customer requirements into credible architectures, pilots, and repeatable engagement models.

What You Bring

AI Expertise: Proven experience designing, prototyping, and deploying enterprise AI/ML or GenAI solutions, with the ability to operate beyond proof-of-concept environments.
AI & Data Architecture: Strong experience across data preparation, ingestion, transformation, retrieval pipelines, embeddings, vectorization, and modern enterprise data architectures.
GenAI and Retrieval Expertise: Practical experience with RAG, knowledge graphs, vector databases, chunking strategies, retrieval optimization, model integration, and evaluation methodologies.
Model & Retrieval Understanding: Strong understanding of how model selection, inference, embeddings, retrieval and evaluation affect the design of enterprise AI data platforms. You do not need to be a model developer or data scientist.
Production AI Experience: Understanding of MLOps/LLMOps, observability, deployment automation, model and data lifecycle management, performance tuning, reliability, and operationalization.
Modern AI Platform Awareness: Strong understanding of the infrastructure and platforms supporting modern AI environments, including cloud, Kubernetes, GPU-enabled architectures, storage, and networking. Deep infrastructure engineering expertise is not required.
Hands-On Technical Credibility: Ability to move comfortably between architecture and implementation, prototype solutions, diagnose technical challenges, and make sound trade-offs when an initial approach does not work.
Professional Services Experience: Experience working directly with enterprise customers, rapidly characterizing ambiguous requirements, defining practical delivery paths, and progressing engagements from discovery through pilot and production.
Cross-Functional Technical Leadership: Ability to establish credibility with senior technical stakeholders and bring together Product, Engineering, Sales, Services, partners, and customers around a common technical direction.

ShotQuality is a leader in AI-driven sports data extraction, combining advanced computer vision and data science to transform video feeds into granular player tracking data and predictive insights. With 20,000+ games processed across 15+ leagues, ShotQuality turns raw video into actionable intelligence. Job Overview:
We are hiring a Quantitative Data Scientist to build the features and predictive models behind ShotQuality's real-time sports products. You will turn raw event, tracking, and market data into signals, test whether they improve on market prices, and get the ones that work into production. This role sits between our data science team and our live products, so you will see your models used in real time by market-facing clients during live games. The ideal candidate comes from a trading background and is energized by fast-moving markets.

Responsibilities:

Feature Engineering:
Design, build, and maintain features from play-by-play, player tracking, and pricing data that improve predictive accuracy.
Predictive Modeling:
Develop and refine probability models for in-game and pregame outcomes, with a focus on calibration and real-world performance.
Market Analysis:
Study how prices move around in-game events and identify where our models add information beyond current market prices.
Backtesting and Evaluation:
Build rigorous backtests that measure whether a model or signal holds up out of sample, against closing lines and live market prices.
Research to Production:
Partner with engineering to move models from notebook to live, low-latency pipelines, and monitor them once they are running.
Performance Analysis:
Track model performance over time, diagnose drift or degradation, and report findings clearly to leadership.
Client Support:
Handle requests from sophisticated, market-facing clients with fast, well-reasoned analysis.

The Role is for Candidates Who: 

Have a background in trading, market making, or quantitative research and get excited about finding an edge in live markets
Have built predictive models that were evaluated on real outcomes and real prices, not just a held-out test set
Enjoy the feature engineering grind and can explain which features mattered and why
Think in probabilities and expected value, and care about calibration, not just accuracy
Move fast, ship quickly, and iterate based on what the data shows
Adapt quickly when priorities shift and are comfortable working without a fixed playbook
Are comfortable with unstructured hours that follow the sports calendar, including live games on nights and weekends﻿

The Role is NOT for Candidates Who:

Have only coursework or Kaggle-style modeling experience
Aren't genuinely interested in prediction markets and the sports betting space
Prefer pure research with no path to production
Need a rigid structure or a predictable 9-to-5 schedule
Are looking for a fully remote role

Requirements:

2+ years of professional experience in quantitative research, trading, or data science, ideally at a trading firm, sportsbook, or prediction market
Strong foundation in statistics and probability, including model calibration and evaluation
Proficiency in Python (pandas, TensorFlow, NumPy, scikit-learn or similar) and SQL
Hands-on experience with gradient boosting, regression, and time-series or sequential modeling
Experience designing backtests and avoiding leakage and overfitting
Ability to communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related quantitative field
Willingness to be available during some nights and weekends of live games (as necessary)

Nice to Have:

Experience with pricing, market making, or market microstructure in sports betting or prediction markets
A track record of building and running your own models in live markets
Experience with sports data, player tracking data, or play-by-play data
Experience deploying models to real-time or low-latency systems
Exposure to AWS or GCP, Docker, and workflow orchestration tools

Description

TL;DR
Kharon is seeking a full-time New York City-based Solutions Architect. This role requires in-office attendance at least 3 days a week.

Kharon's sanctions and risk intelligence helps businesses screen out bad actors. That only matters if it lands inside the systems where decisions get made. You'll be our first Solutions Architect, part integration architect and part investigative builder, designing imaginative ways to embed Kharon's data into clients' screening tools, onboarding flows, and homegrown applications. You'll draw on the whole tool chest, from established playbooks and runbooks to AI-powered prototypes, and take clients from "we should do this" to "we did it."

Responsibilities

Implementations from design to go-live. You'll own client integrations across flat file, API, and MCP, from the first solution design session to launch, working alongside our technical account managers.
Technical discovery with Sales. You'll be the technical voice in early client conversations, turning a messy workflow into a clear scope and a Solution Design Document people still reference a year later.
Proofs of concept that move decisions. You'll scope and build POCs, using tools like Claude Code when they help, so clients can see exactly how Kharon will work in their environment.
Integrations that stay healthy. After launch, you'll own technical support and troubleshooting so live clients keep running smoothly.
The client's voice in the product. You'll bring what you learn in discovery and delivery back to Product in a form that shapes what we build next.
RFPs and security reviews. You'll draft the technical, solution design, and security sections of RFPs and client security questionnaires.

Qualifications

You've sat with B2B clients, run technical discovery, and designed the integration that came out of it.
You build working things yourself: scripts, API calls, data checks, prototypes. AI coding tools are welcome; you know how to check their work.
You understand REST APIs (auth, pagination, error handling), flat file or batch exchange (SFTP, schemas, validation), and MCP, and you've worked hands-on with MCP servers or tools. You can explain when each pattern fits. You use SQL to sanity-check data and work in a scripting language, ideally Python.
You write technical documents people rely on after the meeting ends.
You've owned delivery on at least some engagements, keeping timelines and stakeholders on track.

About the team

The Implementations team is new, and you'll be the first Solutions Architect on it. You'll work closely with our Director of Implementations, technical account managers, Sales, Customer Success, and Product. That means you'll help write the playbook, not just follow it, and your work will shape how the team operates as it grows in 2027. We're still building process, so you'll need to be comfortable making good calls where there isn't a precedent yet.

About Kharon

Kharon is a highly disruptive and incredibly innovative organization that navigates risk at the intersection of global security threats + international commerce.

What does that mean? Great question.

Operating at the nexus of global security, Kharon is on a mission to revolutionize the current landscape. We take really complex data as it relates to global security and empower our clients to not only understand the risk associated with their potential business relationships but to operationalize that data so that they can make the best and most informed decisions possible. From financial crimes and sanctions to export controls and threat identifications, our tools optimize protection against the types of risks that could otherwise be incredibly dangerous and excessively costly to any business. Serving many of today’s leading global financial and multinational institutions, Kharon products are the most powerful in the space with a precision and depth that is absolutely unparalleled.

When you look at any major global crisis event, we’re providing intelligence that’s at the heart of those circumstances. We connect the dots in a way that’s meaningful. Now, we’re experiencing unprecedented growth. As the world continues to evolve in complexity, so too does the demand for our products. Given the significance of our work and the increasing global reliance on our insights, we are looking for a Solutions Architect to join us as we work to shape the way businesses perceive and navigate global risks.

To the right person, this will be the perfect kind of challenge. Our mission is compelling, our product is powerful, and we’re growing at a rate that makes us unstoppable. If you’re looking to be surrounded by people who will inspire you to think and challenge you to grow then look no further. Our team is made up of some of the most visionary and uncompromising individuals you will ever encounter. We don’t take ourselves seriously but we’re serious about the work we do and there is absolutely no slowing us down.

To Keep That Momentum Going, We Do Our Very Best To Make Sure That Each And Every Team Member Is Completely Taken Care Of. We’re Nothing Without Our People And We Strive To Offer a Package That Reflects That. As a Kharon Team Member, You Can Expect

Fully sponsored medical, dental, and vision insurances
FSA program for both medical and dependent care
Long term disability
401k + Roth with matching and immediate vesting
Flexible paid time off + 11 paid holidays

The base salary range at Kharon is set between $130,000 to $160,000. Please note that this figure does not necessarily include potential bonuses, commissions, benefits, or equity that may be part of the overall compensation package.

If interested in pursuing this position, please visit www.kharon.com/careers to apply.

Kharon is an equal opportunity employer. Kharon is committed to cultivating and maintaining a workplace that is free from harassment and discrimination. new_jobs.title: Forward Deployed Integrations Engineer
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

As a Forward Deployed Integrations Engineer
at Coursedog, you'll embed directly with our most strategic customers to own their SIS integration from start to finish, working closely with Engineering, Technical Services, our new Integrations Center of Excellence, and each customer's IT and registrar teams. You'll be responsible for getting integrations live correctly and on plan, protecting the live data they depend on, and turning what you learn in the field into repeatable playbooks and product improvements. The work balances hands-on execution with long-term thinking, and customer-by-customer problem solving with building solutions that scale. This role is well-suited for someone who takes ownership of hard technical problems, enjoys being the trusted technical voice in high-stakes deployments, and is motivated by helping institutions get more from Coursedog while making the platform better for every customer that follows.

If you're excited by complex SIS integration challenges across Banner, Colleague/Ethos, Workday, PeopleSoft, Jenzabar, and Anthology, and want to help strengthen the integrated data foundation that powers every Coursedog product, this is a chance to do meaningful work at real scale.

This position offers a competitive base salary between $90,000 - $110,000
, based on experience and qualifications. The role also includes a performance-based variable compensation component, bringing total on-target earnings (OTE) to $110,000–$120,000
when performance objectives are achieved.

What You'll Do

Embed with customer accounts as the hands-on technical owner and builder, working directly with client IT, registrars, and functional leads
Own end-to-end environment provisioning for staging and production, ensuring infrastructure is optimized and ready for integration before data flows begin
Coordinate SIS connectivity setup with the customer's technical team, managing the handshake process where the customer initiates their side and Coursedog establishes bidirectional data flow
Configure, test, and validate SIS integrations across SIS variants: attribute mappings, field wiring (GET/POST), data transformation logic, effective dating, cross-listing, merge thresholds, and conflict handling
Validate data accuracy throughout the integration setup using test harnesses and sample data, identifying and documenting any mapping issues before production load
Migrate institutional data at scale, planning for volume, merge performance, and client-side data readiness
Root-cause merge and integration failures from merge reports and resolve the underlying cause — not just the ticket
Treat write-back with production-grade care: backups, controlled merges, staging/production parity, and rollback discipline (our writes can change live registration data)
Build API-based solutions and automations (REST, JSON, scripting) that unblock adoption and eliminate recurring friction at the configuration layer before it becomes an engineering escalation
Identify and build out custom or non-standard SIS fields that don't fit standard Coursedog mappings, solving customer-specific data architecture needs directly rather than routing to engineering
Conduct technical sessions with customer IT and integration teams to understand their SIS data structures, data quality issues, and integration constraints, then design solutions that align with best practices
Feed the CoE. Document runbooks and reusable playbooks; partner with Product and Engineering (INT / Integrations Pipeline) to turn recurring fixes into product — validation rules, self-serve health checks, merge explainers
Create clear handoff documentation for the Implementation PM and broader team, including integration architecture, validation results, known constraints, and any custom configurations
Drive adoption and referenceability. Forward-deployed accounts carry an explicit reference and product-feedback mandate

What Success Looks Like (first 12 Months)

Your accounts go live correctly and on plan, with fewer post-go-live merge failures
Zero write-back incidents on your accounts
Measurably fewer issues from your accounts reach the engineering escalation queue
A growing library of runbooks and productized fixes contributed back to the CoE
Your accounts become referenceable

Requirements

What You'll Bring

4+ years of experience in data or integration engineering, solutions engineering, or a forward-deployed technical role
Experience building integrations against complex third-party systems of record, ideally SIS platforms such as Banner, Colleague/Ethos, Workday, or PeopleSoft
Expertise in SIS data structures, data mapping, and ETL concepts, with the ability to troubleshoot data flow issues on your own
Strong technical skills with REST APIs, JSON and CSV, SQL, and scripting in Python or JavaScript
Demonstrated rigor with production change control, including taking backups, testing in staging first, and treating live data with care
Ability to design integration solutions in complex institutional environments, balancing best practices with each customer's constraints
Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences, from running a working session with client IT to explaining timelines and roadblocks to functional leaders
Ability to work independently in a remote, fast-moving environment and travel to customer sites as needed
Knowledge of higher education operations, such as registrar, academic scheduling, or curriculum workflows, is a plus
Experience turning repeated manual services work into tooling or product is a plus
A collaborative, customer-first mindset and sound judgment

Nice to Have

Higher education domain experience (registrar, academic scheduling, curriculum workflows) and familiarity with how registration data flows through institutions
Experience at a company running a forward-deployed engineering model
Experience productizing services work (turning repeated manual fixes into tooling)

Not sure if you should apply?
Research shows that women and people from underrepresented backgrounds are less likely to apply unless they meet every qualification listed. At Coursedog, we're focused on finding the best person for the role, and that person may come from a non-traditional background. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement — our evaluation focuses on your ability to thrive in this role and make an impact.

Benefits

About Coursedog

At Coursedog, our mission is simple but ambitious: to break down barriers to student success.

Founded by former college students who were frustrated by outdated academic systems, Coursedog was built to empower higher ed administrators to deliver exceptional educational experiences and make it easier for students to achieve their goals. Since then, we’ve grown into a platform trusted by institutions across the country.

Coursedog is the Intelligent Academic Operations Platform, empowering 400+ colleges and universities to better serve over 3.3 million students. Our platform brings together academic scheduling, curriculum and catalog management, assessment, and workflow automation — all designed to adapt to each institution’s unique needs and remove administrative roadblocks so educators can focus on helping students succeed.

We’re a remote-first, fast-growing company and a Forbes Top 500 U.S. Startup Employer, with a culture that prioritizes engagement, ownership, and impact. If you’re excited about solving meaningful problems, working with thoughtful teammates, and improving education at scale, you’ll feel right at home at Coursedog.

Working at Coursedog

Healthcare, Dental & Vision

We follow a fixed contribution model to promote equity and transparency. Every employee receives the same annual dollar amount to apply toward medical, dental, and vision coverage. This approach gives you the flexibility to choose the plan that best fits your needs, whether that is a base-level option or more comprehensive coverage.

Depending On The Selected Coverage Level, The Company Covers

Employee-only coverage: 99% to 65% of monthly premiums
Employee plus dependents: 77% to 50% of monthly premiums

We partner with Aetna and Guardian, and offer access to best-in-class wellness and support programs, including:

Spring Health (mental health support)
XP Health (vision benefits)
Carrot Fertility (family planning support)
One Medical (primary care)

We also support pre-tax savings through Health Savings Accounts (HSA) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA).

Retirement Planning

To support long-term financial health, we offer a Safe Harbor 401(k) plan from day one of employment. Coursedog provides a 4% employer match on your total compensation (subject to federal limits) each pay period for employees contributing to a tax-advantaged retirement account.

Paid Time Off

We trust our employees to manage their time responsibly. That’s why we offer an unlimited Paid Time Off policy — because flexibility and balance are critical for sustained excellence and personal well-being.

Remote-First Since Inception

We were built for distributed work. Our culture emphasizes flexibility over rigidity, outcomes over hours, and transparency over gatekeeping. We are committed to being a remote-first organization indefinitely, empowering you to work where and how you thrive best.

Equity

As a valued contributor to our collective success, you’ll participate in the upside. All employees are granted equity in the company aligned to your role and tenure. Equity grants are reviewed and adjusted with promotions to reflect your evolving impact.

Paid Parental Leave

Coursedog supports all parents regardless of gender, family structure, or how you became a parent. All parents receive up to 6 weeks of Paid Bonding Leave at 100% of base pay following the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child. Birthing parents receive an additional 6 weeks of Paid Medical Recovery Leave at 100% of base pay to support physical recovery following childbirth — for a total of up to 12 weeks of fully paid leave.

Core Responsibilities

Operationalizing AI PoCs by transforming demos and prototypes into robust, production-grade AI systems.
Deploying SeekrFlow and agent applications intro customer-managed environments, containerizing and orchestrating them across cloud, hybrid, and on-prem deployments (AWS, Azure, GCP, private cloud).

Codifying best practices into reusable playbooks, evaluation frameworks, and deployment accelerators that scale AI adoption across industries.

Capacity to continuously learn, operate independently, and make decisions with minimal guidance.

Enthusiasm for tackling technical challenges creatively using data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.

new_jobs.description:
About the Role

We are looking for a Principal AI Researcher
to join our growing AI team and help build intelligent, production-grade AI systems that solve complex problems at scale.
In this role, you will work closely with product, engineering, and data teams to design, develop, and deploy AI-powered applications, including LLM-based solutions, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and intelligent automation workflows
.
The ideal candidate is hands-on, highly curious, and comfortable working across the full AI development lifecycle—from experimentation and prototyping to production deployment and optimization.

A Day in the Life

You take an idea from paper to prototype to production. If you have only ever done one of those three, this role will stretch you, and we are fine with that if the rest is strong.
You can build the model layer of a real product, not just a model. That means choosing model sizes, composing several models into a working system, and holding a product-level accuracy bar.
You write real code. Python fluently, PyTorch fluently, and enough systems sense to know why your training run is slow.
You design experiments. You state the hypothesis, run the ablation, and report the result that disagrees with you.
You measure things. You are suspicious of results that look good, and you build the eval before you build the model.
You read current research and can tell the difference between a technique that will hold up and one that will not.
You explain your work to people who are not AI engineers, including clinicians and operators who will tell you when your output is wrong.

What You Need

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field. Exceptional BS candidates with substantial research or open-source work will be considered.
Depth beyond coursework: first-author publications at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, or similar; meaningful open-source ML contributions; a research internship at an AI lab; or models you trained and shipped that people actually used.
You have fine-tuned an open-weight model yourself, understand the difference between parameter-efficient and full fine-tuning, and can explain why you chose one.
Strong Python and PyTorch. Familiarity with the current training and serving stack (HuggingFace, FSDP or DeepSpeed, vLLM or SGLang, or equivalents).
Some exposure to multi-GPU training, even at lab scale. You should know what a sharding strategy is and why it matters.
Evidence you can finish things.
You have post-trained models that ran in production and you know what broke.
You have built the model layer behind a real product feature, including fine-tuning at more than one model size and composing multiple models into a system that met a production accuracy and latency bar.
Hands-on multi-node training experience, tens of GPUs at minimum, on models in the tens of billions of parameters or larger.
You have built or substantially owned a data pipeline that fed a real training run, including the unglamorous parts: dedup, filtering, decontamination, format normalization.
You can scope an ambiguous problem into a plan and tell the difference between a research question and an engineering task.
Mentoring or setting direction for other engineers is a plus and will matter more as the team grows.
You have led post-training on models in the hundreds of billions of parameters, on runs spanning hundreds of GPUs, and you owned the outcome rather than a slice of it.
You have designed the complete model architecture behind a shipped product, spanning small, medium, and large models, and made the tier and composition decisions that determined whether it worked economically.
You have made the calls that decide whether a model program works: data mixture, objective design, when to stop a run, when to abandon an approach that a team is emotionally invested in.
Deep familiarity with large-scale distributed training failure modes and the operational discipline that keeps a long run alive.
A public or verifiable record: papers, model releases, systems, or a training program whose results speak for themselves.
You can set a two-to-four-quarter technical direction and then get a team to execute it. You will effectively define what in-house modeling means at Innovaccer.
